content:
support-liaison: heads up — enterprise customer (acct: AcmeCorp) escalated. p95 jumped to ~900ms and p99 to ~3.8s on Dedicated pool eu-west-2a for text-generation API around 16:15 UTC after a ~2x traffic ramp. They reported a handful of 503s and elevated timeouts. Customer impact is ongoing.

jess: ack. any SLO/alerts triggered? link to timeline?

support-liaison: alerts fired: dedicated.pool.latency.p95 and dedicated.pool.latency.p99, and autoscaler.pending_queue_length > 20. forwarding their support logs now.

sre-oncall-bot: Alert summary: pool=dedicated-eu-west-2a p95=920ms p99=3810ms pending_attach=27 active_pods=64 capacity_limit=64

tyler: initial hunch — pool saturated and attach/scale-up lag. can someone check provisioning queue + cloud provider events? Also check latest pool snapshot: which model variant is hot?

anya: digging into metrics — model variant gpt-medium is getting most of traffic (makes sense). Rate doubled around 16:12. Provisioner events show repeated attach failures: 

```
2026-03-15T16:13:11Z WARN attach: failed to attach vm-attach-usr-xx: no available GPU (requested_type=A100)
2026-03-15T16:13:18Z INFO queue: retrying attach in backoff=12s
2026-03-15T16:14:05Z ERROR warmup: model artifact fetch timed out (client 504)
```

tyler: that fetch timeout could explain slow startup (cold GPU). are nodes being provisioned or are kube pods stuck in Pending?

jess: ran quick `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-eu-west-2a | grep Pending` — several pods Pending due to "no nodes available with nvidia.com/gpu" and some in ImagePullBackOff. copying output: 

```
NAME                                           READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
serve-attach-abc123                             0/1     Pending            0          3m
serve-attach-def456                             0/1     PodInitializing    0          2m
warmup-prepull-ghi789                           0/1     ImagePullBackOff   0          4m
```

jess: also seeing cloud provider events: quota reached for GPUs in AZ eu-west-2a (we've been close to limit).

kai: confirmed — quota exhaustion. autoscaler asked for new nodes but cloud returned 429 / rate-limited and some requests queued. that plus artifact fetch failures = long warmup.

support-liaison: customer asks for ETA and any mitigation we can do now. they are sensitive to p99 since UI shows spinner.

tyler: immediate mitigations we can try:
- temporarily route AcmeCorp to another pool/region (eu-west-1) if they accept cross-region latency
- route them to a smaller model variant (gpt-small) to reduce GPU memory and maybe run on existing spare capacity
- increase pool capacity manually (if available GPUs elsewhere) or request quota bump from cloud (takes longer)
- lower autoscaler backoff / increase attach parallelism to speed up retries
- fallback to hosted CPU instance for critical calls (degraded but available)

anya: I'm already spinning up a manual node group in eu-west-2 (type:gpu-large) to attach faster. starting artifact prefetch to reduce model fetch time.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of artifact-prefetch patch started by anya (deploy_id=deploy-8873)

sre-oncall-bot: Note: automated warmup prefetch will pull model artifacts to the node image cache. this reduces ImagePullBackOff during attach.

jess: also set a temporary routing rule in edge: route AcmeCorp traffic to dedicated-eu-west-1 if token indicates acct=AcmeCorp. added config change and paused rollout for verification.

tyler: good. also lower the autoscaler backoff from 12s -> 4s for this pool so retries happen faster (short-lived change). limit concurrency to avoid thundering herd though.

anya: changed backoff to 4s and increased attach parallelism to 6 (was 3). watch metrics.

(10 min pass)

anya: metrics update — pending_attach dropped from 27 -> 6, p95 improved to ~420ms, p99 trending down to ~1.1s. customer reports fewer 503s. warmup prefetch hit rate is 73%.

support-liaison: AcmeCorp confirmed improvement, but want permanent fix and postmortem.

tyler: immediate resolution: manual node group + warmup prefetch + smaller-model routing + backoff tweak. Good. Next tasks for follow-up:
1) automated predictive scaling for customer traffic spikes (owner: jess)
2) improve model artifact distribution (owner: anya) — make prefetch part of node bootstrap for hot models
3) implement graceful fallback policy in control plane to automatically serve a CPU-hosted smaller variant when Dedicated attach latency exceeds threshold (owner: kai)
4) cloud quota monitoring and proactive bump process (owner: tyler)

jess: putting tasks in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/4523 (will add runbook steps).

tyler: postmortem notes — probable root causes: pool capacity saturated by sudden ramp + cloud provider rate limits for GPU provisioning + model artifact fetch failures causing longer warmups. mitigations reduced customer impact.

deploy-bot: deploy deploy-8873 completed to canary; rollout id=8873 status=success

anya: will follow up with logs + short repro recipe for eng-runtime team: steps to reproduce locally: 
1. spike qps to pool with gpt-medium style load (2x normal)
2. throttle cloud-provisioner API to simulate 429s
3. ensure model registry returns delayed responses to simulate artifact fetch timeouts

kai: adding an automation task to check pending_attach > 10 -> temporarily relax routing rules and route specific customer tokens to fallback pool.

support-liaison: customer happy for now, wants SLA credits discussion — escalated to account team.

tyler: thanks all. marking oncall handoff. owners please file full postmortem and link runbook updates.

jess: noted. closing thread when GH ticket and runbook PRs are created.
